opening.headline: How can we record and decide whether or not to allow use cases brought by the field, on what basis and on what basis?
body: Governance officials frequently receive review requests asking, “Can I use AI for this task?” Even if the same model is used, the answer will vary depending on how it is used, so if each person in charge makes a decision based on different standards, the results are likely to be inconsistent.

In this class, you will learn a four-step decision process: case description, policy response, classification, and recording. In three cases, we will see how permission, conditional permission, and prohibition are different, and we will follow the explanation of how to write the conditions of conditional permission in verifiable sentences and the judgment record format.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Use cases can be matched to policy items
The basis for decision to allow, conditionally allow, or prohibit can be evaluated.

screens.title: Should we allow use cases brought by the field?
screens.lead:
Read the three requests from the field and first think about what conclusion you would draw from each.

Policy base date: 2026-10-23. Distinguish between the version currently in effect and the version scheduled to be implemented. Anthropic has released the 2026-11-12 enforcement version, so you should check again for changes in the enforcement date and high-risk areas and disclosure obligations before actual operation.

visual.alt: Illustration showing three requests and a question mark next to each request.
labels: Evaluate applicant documents and select interview candidates
Automatically generate favorable reviews of new products and post them on shopping malls

paragraphs: Request A states that they would like to summarize company meeting minutes into a model. Request B states that they would like to select interviewees by evaluating applicant documents as a model. Request C is that you want to automatically create favorable reviews for new products and post them on the shopping mall. All three requests will use the same model, but the conclusions will not be the same.

The person in charge must say one of permissive, conditional permissible, or prohibited in each case, and the conclusion must be accompanied by evidence. Conclusions made based on intuition are difficult to explain consistently when the same case comes up again.

The goal of this class is to make decisions based on procedures, not intuition. The process consists of four steps: accurately describing the case, matching it to policy items, categorizing it, and recording the rationale.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: Among the three requests, is there any that cannot be granted even with conditions attached? Check with evidence in class.

screens.outro: First, let me recall an experience I had when I was asked to review something.

screens.title: Have you ever received a review request?
screens.lead: When you select a question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. The answer will not be submitted, so think about your experience first and then check.

items.prompt: Have you ever been asked to review a business use case?
items.answer: Requests are usually short, one or two sentences long. Since it is impossible to determine what the data is and who uses the results and how they are used, the case must first be described in detail.

items.prompt: Where did you write down the basis for your judgment at that time?
items.answer: It often ends with a messenger or verbal response. If no evidence remains, it will be difficult to explain the same decision again when the policy is revised or the person in charge changes.

items.prompt: What did you do when it was unclear whether it was allowed or prohibited?
items.answer: Ambiguous cases can be conditionally accepted or reserved without being dichotomous. In this lesson, we will put together the three classifications and how to use them. When putting something on hold, it's better to leave the question as to what's missing. Once you receive the answer, you can continue judging on the same record.

screens.outro: We will now look at the four steps of the decision process in turn.

screens.title: Judgment process four steps
screens.lead: Select the right arrow to see the decision process step by step. We guide you through each step and what the deliverables are.

steps.title: Step 1: Describe the case
steps.body: Write down who inputs what data, what output is produced, and who decides what as a result. The output is a paragraph describing the case. If data and determinants are missing from this paragraph, the policy item will not be found in later steps. Classification depends on usage rather than industry, so it is important to write down usage accurately. For example, if you write just one line, ‘Document evaluation,’ you cannot know whether a person has finalized it, so you must also write down the person who confirmed it.

steps.title: Step 2: Match policy items
steps.body: The described examples are found in the policies of the three companies. Check whether it touches a prohibited category, a restricted category, or a high-risk area. The output is a list of touched items and their document locations. Find documents from all three companies, but make sure to write down any items that are specific to one company. If nothing is touched, this can be considered acceptable in policy terms.

steps.title: Step 3: Sort
steps.body: Decide whether to allow, allow with conditions, or prohibit and write the reason in one or two sentences. If it touches a common prohibition, it is prohibited; if it touches a restricted category, but opens if conditions are met, it is conditionally permitted. If it is a conditional acceptance, the conditions are confirmed at this stage.

steps.title: Step 4: Write it down
steps.body: Leave supporting documents, dates of versions read, conditions, and reviewers. As policies are revised, the date of the revision will be used as a basis for reopening the decision at a later date. The records serve as a precedent when similar requests are made. If you follow the four steps, the same decision will be made in the same case even if the person in charge changes.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen the procedure, let's apply it to three cases one by one.

screens.title: Cases A and B: Acceptance and conditional acceptance
screens.lead: The table below organizes Cases A and B according to the decision procedure. Read each line and find out why the judgments are different even when using the same model.

data.caption: Comparison of decisions between cases A and B
columns: Case A: Summary of meeting minutes
Case B: Evaluation of applicant documents
rows: An employee records the company meeting minutes, receives a summary, and uses it as reference material.
The human resources team submits applicant documents and selects interviewees based on the evaluation results.
It does not come under any prohibited or restricted categories.
Employment is considered a high-risk area by Google and OpenAI. If AI makes a decision alone, it reaches an automatic decision without human supervision.
There are no conditions on the policy side. However, I leave a note to separately check the data conditions included in the meeting minutes.
The structure has been changed to one where a person makes the final decision, and separate prohibited functions such as emotional inference are not used for evaluation.
This is not a usage that the policy prevents.
The decision is made more by automatic decision-making without supervision than by field.
data.notes: Case A is a policy-wise permit and data handling is a separate check. Looking at the two examples side by side, it becomes clear that usage rather than discipline separates the classification. Even if the same HR team uses the same tool, the judgment will vary depending on who makes the decision. If meeting minutes contain customer or non-public information, they must follow data handling standards separate from policy decisions. In Case B, even if it is the same tool, changing the decision structure changes the design that touches prohibition to conditional permission.

screens.outro: We will also check for cases of bans that do not open even if conditions are added.

screens.title: Case C: Ban decision
screens.lead: When you select each item, the basis for decision for Case C will unfold. Find out what policy language it is based on and what it proposes when it is banned.

items.answer: Automatically generating favorable reviews for new products and posting them on shopping malls is a false review that deceives consumers. Reviews are read with the assumption that they are the actual buyer's experience, so creating them is a deception in itself. This judgment does not change no matter how natural the model's sentences are. The higher the quality, the more difficult it is for consumers to spot a fake, which increases the problem.

Anthropic policies list prohibited activities that use fake accounts, fake people, and fake reviews to mislead people. Fake reviews are listed as examples, leaving little room for interpretation. If an example is found directly in the document, the location of the phrase is recorded in the decision record and used as a basis.

Our policies prohibit fraudulent and deceptive activities, as well as misrepresenting created content as human-generated. This is where posting favorable reviews as if they were written by actual buyers goes a long way. It is important to note that even if the wording of the two companies is different, they reach the same conclusion.

items.prompt: Will it be resolved if conditions are attached?
items.answer: It doesn't resolve. This is because human review does not change the fact that the review is fake. These prohibitions are responded to not as conditions but as alternatives. You can summarize actual buyer reviews or suggest ways to write a text asking buyers to leave a review. A ban ruling does not block the purpose of the requesting department, which is to help sales with trustworthy reviews, but only the means.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen the three decisions, let's continue with an explanation of how to write conditions for conditional acceptance.

screens.title: Explanation: How to write conditions for conditional acceptance
screens.lead: Click the toggle to compare when the same condition is written vaguely and when it is written specifically.

states.label: ambiguous conditions
states.body: “Human review” is empty of who will see what, when, and when. I don't know how to "be mindful of personal information". “Leaving a record” does not specify what or where to leave a record. These conditions are interpreted differently by each person who reads them, and there is no way to check whether they have been followed, so they are limited to formal clues. It is difficult to say that the conditions were followed even when an accident occurred. It is because of this ambiguity that conditional permission is in fact operated like unconditional permission.

states.label: specific conditions
states.body: If you write something like, “The HR team member reads the list of candidates generated by AI and directly confirms the disqualification process,” the subject and action are clear. “Names and contact information are removed before entry” is a verifiable action. There are established record items to “write the use case number, supporting document, version date, and contact person in the adjudication record.” Every condition must have someone checking it and when it needs to be checked. This will allow you to check whether the conditions were actually met. After writing the conditions, check again to see if the reader may interpret them differently. The timing of inspection can be determined before introduction, during regular inspection during operation, or when revising policy. If you write down the confirmation method like this, the condition becomes not just a declaration but an operating procedure.

screens.outro: Now that you know how to write conditions, let's complete the judgment record form.

screens.title: Commentary: Judgment Record Form
screens.lead: Fill out Case B's decision record in column order on the form. Select the next arrow to follow the columns as they are populated.

steps.title: Identification and Examples
steps.body: Write down the use case number, the requesting department, and write a one-paragraph description of the case. Case B includes information that the HR team inputs the applicant documents and selects interviewees based on the evaluation results, and who the final decision maker is. At this time, the wording in the request should not be copied as is, but should be rewritten with the information necessary for the decision.

steps.title: Policy items and classifications
steps.body: Write down the corresponding policy items. High-risk provisions in the employment sector and automatic decision-making provisions without human supervision. In the category box, write “Conditional Acceptance” and add the reason in one sentence. The reason is that although the field is high risk, the final decision is made by a person.

steps.title: Conditions and grounds
steps.body: In the condition field, write down specific conditions. The HR staff reads the list of candidates and directly confirms the elimination, and does not use the emotional inference function. In the supporting document field, enter the document name and clause location.

steps.title: Edition date and reviewer
steps.body: Write down the date and reviewer of the edition you read. Once the policy is revised, it will become the basis for reopening existing awards. If it doesn't fit anywhere: Allowed, Conditional, or Prohibited, leave the classification on hold and ask additional questions.

steps.title: set a precedent
steps.body: The completed record serves as a precedent for subsequent similar cases. If you manage your record forms as shared documents, you can search and find them right away. If another department requests a similar evaluation tool, they can refer to this record first and make a new judgment only on what has changed. Remember, the purpose is to check for differences, not to copy precedents.

screens.outro: Now that we have the format, let's summarize the key points.

screens.title: Key takeaway: Decisions come with supporting documentation and conditions
screens.lead: The contents of this class are organized into four categories: procedures, classifications, conditions, and records.

paragraphs: The adjudication process involves four steps: case description, policy response, classification, and recording. When describing a case, do not omit who inputs what data, creates what output, and who makes the decisions. Classification depends on usage rather than industry.

There are three classifications: permitted, conditionally permitted, and prohibited, and if it doesn't fit into any of them, it's withheld. Conditional acceptance is when conditions are met, such as a person's final confirmation. Bans that cannot be lifted with conditions, like fake reviews, offer an alternative.

Conditions are written specifically to include the person and point of view. We record the decision with supporting documentation and version date, and reopen the decision when the policy is revised. Accumulated records serve as precedents and increase consistency of decisions. When accumulating records, organize not only permissions and prohibitions but also conditional permission conditions so that they can be searched. When using precedents, we first compare the differences between the previous case and the current case, check whether the difference affects the policy item, and then apply the same decision.

When starting your judgment, check the following three things: Does the case description contain data and decision makers, are the policy items being reached written with the document location, and is there a person and time to check for each condition? If these three things are in place, other people in charge can read it and reach the same conclusion. These three items can also be used as inspection items after completing the judgment. If missing items are found during the inspection, they are corrected before confirming the decision. It is better if the inspector is different from the judge. The inspection results are also recorded in the same record.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: If a condition is not confirmed by whom or when it is confirmed, the condition has no effect.

checks.intro: Check the decision logic for case B for yourself. This confirmation is not logged.
checks.q: How do you classify the review of applicant documents in a structure where the HR team looks at the list of candidates ranked by AI and directly confirms rejection?
options: Prohibited. Because employment is a high-risk field.
Allowed. Doesn't fit into any policy category
Conditional acceptance. It is a high-risk field, but people make the final decision.
On hold. Policy documents cannot be used to judge
checks.explain: Employment is a high-risk field, but the problem is that AI alone determines it. Once the person finalizes it, it becomes a conditional acceptance.

wrong.0: The field alone is not prohibited; the manner in which it is used is the criterion.
wrong.1: It is not permitted without conditions as it falls under a restricted category as it is an employment field.
wrong.3: It can be ruled as a high-risk clause and an automatic decision clause.

checks.correctFeedback: That's right. Because the structure is such that decisions are confirmed by people, conditional permission is appropriate.
checks.incorrectFeedback: You may have judged based on the name of the field alone. Pay attention to who finalizes decisions.

checks.intro: Match the three use cases with the verdict. For each case on the left, choose the appropriate decision on the right.
checks.q: Pair your verdict with the following use cases:
left: After ranking applicants, a person makes the final decision.
right: Conditional acceptance: Structure that is finalized by humans
DON’T: Provide summaries of actual buyer reviews as an alternative.
Accepted: Separate note for data conditions
checks.explain: Classification depends on usage rather than industry. False reviews are a ban that cannot be lifted even if conditions are attached.
checks.correctFeedback: All three cases have been linked correctly. It turns out that there are different classifications depending on how they are used.
checks.incorrectFeedback: Some connections are off. First, divide the cases into cases where conditions can be solved and cases where conditions cannot be solved.

checks.intro: Check out how to write conditions. Just choose the condition that is easiest to check.
checks.q: What is the most appropriate condition for conditional permission?
options: ‘A person in charge of the human resources team reviews the list of candidates and directly confirms the disqualification process.’
‘Be careful to ensure that the department in charge sufficiently reviews people.’
‘Be mindful of personal information and handle input data carefully’
‘The decision process will be recorded as much as possible.’
checks.explain: Conditions must include who, when, and what to do to be confirmed.

wrong.1: 'Things to note' is empty as to who will see what.
wrong.2: There is no way to 'carefully' check. It must be specifically written, such as removing name and contact information.
wrong.3: There is no standard for ‘as much as possible’. Record items and contact persons must be specified.

checks.correctFeedback: That's correct. It is a condition that can be checked to see if the subject and action are clear and have been observed.
checks.incorrectFeedback: There is no way to check whether this sentence was followed. Find sentences that contain who does what.

glossary.def: A decision is allowed if certain conditions are met. The conditions and the person responsible for verification are specified.
The review sequence leads to case description, policy response, classification, and documentation.
This is a recorded judgment case. This will be taken into consideration when evaluating similar requests.

misconceptions.myth: If the industry is allowed, the case is also allowed.
misconceptions.fact: Depending on how it is used, the same industry has different judgments. The policy looks at usage, not industry.

misconceptions.myth: The conditions of conditional acceptance are formal provisos.
misconceptions.fact: If the conditions do not specify who or when to confirm them, they are not effective. It must be written specifically so that it can be confirmed.
If the policy is revised or the case changes, we will reopen the adjudication. This is why the edition date is recorded.

closing.lead: We recapitulate the key points of this lesson.
points: Judgment is made in the following order: case description, policy response, classification, and recording.
Conditions are written in detail, including people and time points.
Keep the source document and edition date in your records.
There are three classifications: permitted, conditionally permitted, and prohibited.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for your own reflection only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: How are use case verdicts recorded in our organization now, and how do we record them when the same case comes up again?
